title: Prince William supervisors unanimously cut the by-right data center overlay from 9,698 to 3,654 acres (zoning text amendment)

facts.instrument: zoning text amendment (ZTA) to the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay
facts.grace_period: 90 days for developers to file applications before the new overlay takes effect; motion to cut it to zero failed 5-3
facts.event_date_basis: Bisnow article dated Sunday 2026-09-20 says the vote is on 'Tuesday' (the board's upcoming Tuesday meeting), i.e. Tuesday 2026-09-22; Bisnow's own text says 'on Tuesday'

summary: The board unanimously approved a zoning text amendment that largely removes by-right data center development by shrinking the overlay district. Data centers remain permitted, but projects outside the smaller overlay need full review.
source_title: Bisnow — Prince William County Drastically Shrinks By Right Data Center Map
verbatims: unanimously approved a zoning text amendment that largely eliminates by right data center development
The ZTA proposed to reduce the size of the overlay from 9,698 acres to 3,654 acres
The supervisors voted 5-3 against a separate motion
notes: Not a moratorium: this is a by-right to special-review change (the Loudoun lesson). Bisnow says the ZTA 'proposed' the acreage per a Planning Commission report; the final adopted acreage is not confirmed. The 'Tuesday' date is inferred from the Sunday 2026-09-20 article date. Two secondary sources (JD Supra, WJLA preview) were not used as citations. A search summary claimed Loudoun approved a 12-month moratorium on new data center applications; NOT recorded here, and it contradicts the Virginia law note in the seed. Check Loudoun's own record before any entry.

title: Fort Wayne councilwoman introduces year-long pause on council's own data center actions

facts.instrument: two ordinances (introduced by Councilwoman Rohli Booker), plus an advisory committee
facts.scope: restricts only the council's own actions; city economic development and planning staff remain free to work with companies; does not affect the already operational Google data center
facts.vote: all present members supported introduction; final vote not yet found
facts.event_date_basis: WBOI (2026-09-09) and Journal Gazette (2026-09-08) say introduction was at Tuesday night's council meeting, i.e. Tuesday 2026-09-08

summary: Fort Wayne's council introduced a one-year pause covering only its own legislative actions on data centers, plus an advisory committee. The proposal does not bind the executive branch or private development, so it is not a moratorium on construction.
source_title: Journal Gazette — Councilwoman proposes pause on new Fort Wayne data centers, board for large developments
verbatims: Booker emphasized that the moratorium on data centers would restrict only the council's actions, leaving city economic development and planning officials free to work with companies interested in Fort Wayne.
It will not affect the already operational data center.
notes: Typed as policy because the pause binds only the council (Loudoun/Marshall-style board-docket rule). Media call it a moratorium; the record says what it is. The BACKLOG lead says the vote was postponed to mid-October; this is NOT verified by any fetched source. Companion WBOI verbatim also probe-HIT: 'introduced ordinances that would put a year-long moratorium on construction of data centers'. The WBOI wording is media shorthand and should not be used as the scope statement.

title: Kalamazoo City Commission unanimously approves one-year moratorium on data center and related applications

facts.duration: one year, scheduled to last until 2027-08-16
facts.could_end_early: if new or amended city regulations take effect
facts.follow_up: Planning Commission voted unanimously on 2026-09-03 to recommend a zoning text amendment that would make the moratorium part of the zoning code (per search summary; not fetched)

summary: The Kalamazoo City Commission unanimously adopted a one-year pause on accepting and processing applications for data centers, battery storage, crypto mining and AI data centers. It is scheduled to run to 2027-08-16 unless replaced by regulations.
source_title: Watershed Voice — Kalamazoo City Commission passes one-year data center moratorium
verbatims: Commissioners unanimously approved the resolution on August 17
The moratorium is scheduled to last until August 16, 2027
notes: Out-of-band: a related-article blurb on the same page gives an end date of 2027-10-05, conflicting with the article's 2027-08-16. The record uses the article body. The search result said an Oct 5 2026 commission vote on the zoning amendment; NOT verified and not recorded as a finding. The Oct 5 date may be a misreading of the Oct 5 Kalamazoo commission schedule.

title: Inver Grove Heights council passes one-year data center construction moratorium 3-2

facts.event_date_basis: Fox 9 article published 2026-06-26 (a Friday). The same article also says the meeting was originally set for 'Monday night' and gives 'Friday' for the start; the vote date is therefore not certain. The date used is the publication date.
facts.trigger: proposed 54,000 sq ft (article says ~55,000 sq ft) data center on Carmen Avenue East by QLevr; developer threatened suit
facts.followup_2026_09_14: council voted Monday 2026-09-14 to exempt the QLevr project from the moratorium; moratorium remains for other projects (MPR, 2026-09-15); lawsuit to be dismissed without city damages

summary: Inver Grove Heights council voted 3-2 for a one-year pause on data center construction while the city studies impacts. The moratorium was passed while a developer had threatened to sue.
source_title: Fox 9 — Data center moratorium passed by Inver Grove Heights City Council
verbatims: the council voted 3-2 to pass a moratorium on data center construction
notes: Event date (2026-06-26) is before the brief's window; included because the unit's BACKLOG lead names it and it is untracked. Fox 9's own text is internally inconsistent (Friday vs Monday), so the vote date needs the council minutes. The QLevr square footage and 2026-04-27 application date from the search summary were NOT found on the page and are NOT recorded. The MPR phrase 'The one-year moratorium remains in place for any other data center projects in the city' is HIT for the follow-up finding.

title: Inver Grove Heights exempts QLevr data center from its moratorium to end developer lawsuit threat

facts.site: QLevr proposed data center, Carmen Avenue East (no project record tracked)
facts.condition: QLevr's attorneys offered to dismiss the lawsuit without the city paying damages
facts.next_step: council to consider a site plan application later in September 2026 (outcome not found)

summary: The council voted on 2026-09-14 to exempt the QLevr proposal from the moratorium after the developer's attorneys offered to dismiss a lawsuit without city damages. The moratorium still applies to other data center projects in the city.
source_title: MPR News — Inver Grove Heights exempts data center project from city moratorium
verbatims: The Inver Grove Heights City Council voted Monday to allow a data center proposal to continue despite a moratorium on such projects.
The one-year moratorium remains in place for any other data center projects in the city.
notes: Attaches to no tracked project; the QLevr site needs its own Project record before it can carry this update. The MPR article says the lawsuit could cost the city at least $20 million; the search summary's $150 million claim is not on this page and is not recorded.
